**1.** (3 pt each) Set up the design matrix $\mathbf{X}$ and $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ vector for each of the following regression models (assume $i = 1, 2, 3, 4$):

**(a)**
$$Y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{i1} + \beta_2 X_{i1} X_{i2} + \epsilon_i$$

*Answer:*

**(b)**
$$\log Y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{i1} + \beta_2 X_{i2} + \epsilon_i$$

*Answer:*

**(c)**
$$Y_i = \beta_1 X_{i1} + \beta_2 X_{i2} + \beta_3 X_{i1}^2 + \epsilon_i$$

*Answer:*

**(d)**
$$\sqrt{Y_i} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{i1} + \beta_2 \log_{10} X_{i2} + \epsilon_i$$

**3.** (3 pt each) A simple analysis using R of the commercial properties data is shown below. The dataset contains information on rental rates and building characteristics for 81 commercial properties, with variables: `rental` (rental rate per sq ft per year), `age` (age in years), `expenses` (operating expenses and taxes), `vacancy` (vacancy rate), and `footage` (total square footage). The pairs plot is shown in Figure 1 and the diagnostic plots for `fit1` are shown in Figure 2.

```

> pairs(a, labels = c("rental", "age", "expenses", "vacancy", "footage"))

> rental   <- a[, 1]
> age      <- a[, 2]
> expenses <- a[, 3]
> vacancy  <- a[, 4]
> footage  <- a[, 5]

> fit <- lm(rental ~ age + expenses + vacancy + footage)
> summary(fit)
```
